title: [15] Deploy self-hosted coturn TURN server on the Oracle VPS
why_we_need_this: Video calls fail for users behind restrictive NATs (e.g. Russian ISPs) because there is no TURN relay server. Hosted TURN services (Metered.ca) cost $99+/month for usable bandwidth. The Oracle VPS that already hosts Shmax (raskolniktv.mooo.com) has free bandwidth — running coturn there costs $0 extra and provides unlimited relay traffic for 1:1 calls.
acceptance_criteria:
1. coturn is installed and running on the Oracle VPS as a systemd service (auto-starts on reboot)
2. coturn listens on UDP/3478 (STUN+TURN), TCP/3478 (TURN TCP), and TLS/443 or TLS/5349 (TURNS) — TLS transport is mandatory for passing through restrictive firewalls
3. A valid TLS certificate is configured for TURNS (can reuse the existing Let's Encrypt cert from nginx, or generate a separate one for the TURN subdomain)
4. Static credentials (long-term-credential mechanism) are configured in turnserver.conf — username/password stored only in the conf file on the VPS, not in the repo
5. Oracle VPS firewall (iptables/nftables + Oracle Cloud security list) allows inbound UDP 3478, TCP 3478, TCP 5349 (or 443), and UDP 49152–65535 (relay range)
6. Shmax backend env vars are set: STUN_SERVERS, TURN_SERVER_URL, TURN_SERVER_USERNAME, TURN_SERVER_CREDENTIAL pointing to the coturn instance
7. Verified: `turnutils_uclient` (or browser test) confirms TURN allocation succeeds from an external network
8. coturn does not interfere with existing nginx on port 443 — either use port 5349 for TURNS, or a dedicated IP/subdomain, or share 443 via SNI
9. Log rotation is configured for coturn logs so the VPS disk doesn't fill up
10. The VPS hosts multiple projects — coturn must not degrade performance for other services (set max-bps and total-quota limits in turnserver.conf)
important_constraints:
- The VPS is a shared Oracle Cloud instance hosting multiple projects behind one nginx — coturn must coexist without conflicting on ports or eating all bandwidth
- Do NOT open relay ports wider than necessary — restrict relay-port range in turnserver.conf
- TLS certificate must not break existing nginx HTTPS — prefer port 5349 for TURNS if sharing the same IP/cert is complicated
- Credentials must NOT be committed to the repo — env vars or server-side config only
- coturn should run as a dedicated non-root user
- Oracle Cloud has a separate cloud-level firewall (Security Lists / Network Security Groups) in addition to OS-level iptables — both must be updated
